test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 09 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: One pipe can fill the tank in 7 minutes while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 56 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill three-fourth of the tank?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net efficiency = **Inlet** efficiency − **Outlet** efficiency

Efficiency of **Pipe 1** = 56 ÷ 7 = 8 units/min

Efficiency of **Pipe 2** = 56 ÷ 56 = 1 unit/min

Combined efficiency = 8 − 1 = 7 units/min

Time for 3/4th tank = (3/4 × 56) ÷ 7 = 42 ÷ 7 = 6 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **Filling Pipe** time = 7 min, **Emptying Pipe** time = 56 min

Formula Used: **Total Work** = **Efficiency** × **Time**

⇒ Let **Total Capacity** of tank = LCM(7, 56) = 56 units

⇒ Combined Efficiency of both pipes = 8 − 1 = 7 units/min

⇒ Target volume to fill = 3/4 × 56 = 42 units

⇒ Required Time = 42 ÷ 7 = 6 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

Inlet pipe efficiency is taken as positive (+), while outlet (leakage) pipe efficiency is taken as negative (−).

Net Work Done

If two pipes fill a tank in x and y hours, net work in 1 hour = 1/x + 1/y. If one fills and one empties, net work = 1/x − 1/y.</p
